title: implement BatchNorm2d

atoms.evidence: register_buffer for running_mean/running_var; EMA update: self.running_mean = (1-momentum)*self.running_mean + momentum*mean
weight initialized to ones, bias to zeros, applied as x_normed * weight + bias after normalization
if self.training: compute batch stats and update running; else: use running stats
reshape (num_features,) -> (1, num_features, 1, 1) to broadcast against (batch, channels, H, W); explicit tip in exercise about broadcasting
einops.rearrange('channels -> 1 channels 1 1') to make stats broadcastable; reshape via einops
self.register_buffer('running_mean', t.zeros(...)) — non-learnable state that participates in state_dict but not in optimization; a NEW atom not in seed vocab

notes: Densest exercise so far: 9 atoms in one ~25-line forward. Seed's prediction for this exercise was 100% accurate (no false positives) — the batchnorm cluster was well-scoped. One new atom proposal: register-buffer (distinct from nn-parameter-wrap; for state that should round-trip via state_dict but not be optimized — running stats, attention masks, position encodings, etc). kaiming-uniform-init does NOT appear here (weight=ones, bias=zeros), confirming it's a per-Module choice not a universal pattern.
